title: Closed-complement vanishing for proper pushforward of open extension
statement: Fix a prime $\ell$ and a field $k$ of positive characteristic different from $\ell$; all schemes below are separated of finite type over $k$ and all maps are $k$-morphisms [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Let $\Lambda$ be admissible [sk-def-localizing-closure], with the finite-subextension condensed ring of [sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed] for $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$. Use ordinary unbounded module-object derived categories and total derived pushpull [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], and exact termwise open extension by zero [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-lower-shriek]. Let $r:W\to\overline Y$ be a morphism, $i:Y\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ a quasi-compact open immersion, $U=W\times_{\overline Y}Y$, and $j:U\hookrightarrow W$, $p:U\to Y$ the projections [def-pc-fibre-product; def-weil-open-immersion]. Assume $r$ is proper [def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $c:Z\hookrightarrow\overline Y$ be the reduced closed complement of $i(Y)$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Then for every bounded constructible complex of finite Tor amplitude $A\in\Dctf(U,\Lambda)$ [sk-def-sfb-constructible], $$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq0\quad\text{in }D(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda).$$ This is a statement about the target object alone, with no comparison morphism or localizing-closure conclusion.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation for bounded constructible finite-Tor inputs, before detecting the comparison isomorphism.

proof.text: Put $T=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, with projections $a:T\to W$ and $r_Z:T\to Z$. Base change of the closed immersion $c$ makes $a$ a closed immersion; its underlying closed subset is $r^{-1}(|Z|)$, whose complement is exactly $U=r^{-1}(Y)$. The morphism $j$ is an open immersion by base change of $i$, and is quasi-compact by quasi-compact base change. Base change of properness makes $r_Z$ proper. The closed immersions $c$ and $a$ are proper, hence separated and of finite type; composition with the structure morphisms of $\overline Y$ and $W$ shows that $Z$ and $T$ are separated finite-type $k$-schemes. Thus the square $(a,r_Z,r,c)$ is a proper base-change square inside the standing setting. The scheme $T$ need not be reduced: only its closed underlying subset, complementary to $U$, is used.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation; auxiliary hypotheses expanded explicitly.

proof.text: Apply the mixed-restriction vanishing $i^*j_!=0$ of [lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization] to the complementary immersions $a:T\hookrightarrow W$ and $j:U\hookrightarrow W$. Its quasi-compactness hypothesis holds by step 1. Its coefficients are arbitrary commutative condensed rings, and its derived categories are ordinary unbounded module-object categories, as here. Consequently $a^*j_!A\simeq0$ in $D(T_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},\Lambda)$, without any further boundedness or reducedness assumption.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation; auxiliary hypotheses expanded explicitly.

proof.text:
Set $K=j_!A$. Constructibility: since $j_!$ is exact and applied termwise, $H^q(K)\cong j_!H^q(A)$ for every $q$ [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology], so $K$ is bounded with the bounds of $A$. Each $H^q(A)$ is constructible in the finite-constant-local-model sense of [sk-def-sfb-constructible], hence so is $j_!H^q(A)$ by [lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible] (strata of $U$ together with the reduced complement, zero model on the complement). Thus $K\in\Dbc(W,\Lambda)$ in the sense used by $\Dctf$. A finite constant local model is locally finitely presented [det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model], on the same strata, so $K$ is also bounded constructible in the ring-object sense of [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible] used by the rational base-change node. Tor amplitude: choose a finite Tor interval $[u,v]$ for $A$. For any sheaf $N$ of $\Lambda_W$-modules, the open-immersion derived projection formula gives
$$K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_W}N\simeq j_!\bigl(A\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\Lambda_U}j^*N\bigr).$$
The cartesian-coefficient assertion makes $j^*$ exact, so $j^*N$ is again a sheaf in degree zero. The inner tensor therefore has cohomology only in $[u,v]$, and by exactness of $j_!$ again so does its extension by zero. Thus $K\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation; auxiliary hypotheses expanded explicitly.

proof.text:
Suppose $\Lambda$ is a finite commutative ring killed by a power of $\ell$. Apply clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite] to $r:W\to\overline Y$, $g=c$, $g'=a$, and $p'=r_Z$. Properness and the standing scheme hypotheses hold by step 1, and $K=j_!A$ lies in $\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$ by step 3. It follows that
$$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*a^*j_!A.$$
Both sides are objects of the ordinary unbounded module-object derived category on $Z$.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation; auxiliary hypotheses expanded explicitly.

proof.text:
For $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E$ use clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-integral] on the same square and $K=j_!A\in\Dbc(W,\mathcal O_E)$ from step 3. This also covers $\mathbf Z_\ell$ by taking $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$, whose valuation ring is $\mathbf Z_\ell$. For $\Lambda=E$ or $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, use clause (3) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-rational], again on that square and bounded constructible $K$. The case $\mathbf Q_\ell$ is $E=\mathbf Q_\ell$. These cases and step 4 exhaust the admissible list in [sk-def-localizing-closure]. The algebraic-closure coefficient is throughout the finite-subextension condensed ring fixed in the statement. We obtain in every case
$$c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq R(r_Z)_*a^*j_!A.$$
Only bounded constructible inputs to these theorems are used, with no assertion on a localizing closure.

source.place: Proof (3), closed-complement calculation; auxiliary hypotheses expanded explicitly.

proof.text: Substitute $a^*j_!A\simeq0$ from step 2 into the isomorphism of step 4 or 5. The derived adjunction $r_Z^*\dashv R(r_Z)_*$ implies $R(r_Z)_*0\simeq0$: for every $B$, its adjunction identifies $\operatorname{Hom}(B,R(r_Z)_*0)$ with the singleton $\operatorname{Hom}(r_Z^*B,0)$, so $R(r_Z)_*0$ is terminal and hence isomorphic to the zero object. Thus $c^*Rr_*j_!A\simeq0$, as claimed.

split_report.summary: Expanded the closed-complement calculation into its geometric square, mixed-restriction vanishing, explicit constructibility and Tor-amplitude check, coefficient-by-coefficient proper base change, and preservation of zero by the derived right adjoint. Reused existing nodes throughout; no new nodes or statement changes. Reviewer repair (N5 maintainer reader, 2026-10-21): step 3 now derives constant-local-model constructibility of j_!A from lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible instead of the locally-finitely-presented node lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves.
split_report.blueprint: Realizes exactly the target-object calculation in det-sf-comp-composition-interchange.proof.md, Proof (3), from proper base change along c to vanishing on the inverse-image complement. It does not use the comparison-isomorphism or localizing-extension clauses.

tool_uses.why: Extension by zero preserves constructibility in the finite-constant-local-model sense of sk-def-sfb-constructible (the sense of Dctf and of the base-change inputs); the composition unit gives no such node, and lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves only gives the weaker locally-finitely-presented notion.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-N5-bf4216140 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item, all 6 steps, the report, the source (det-sf-comp-composition-interchange.proof.md Proof (3), main-20261015) and the statement of every cited node. The statement is unchanged from the base and not weakened. It holds in every edge case I tried: U empty, Y=Ybar, U=W, A=0, non-reduced T, zero ring. The delivery creates no new nodes, and there is no cycle and no SGA citation. Step 1 (base-change geometry) is correct. Step 2 is correct: lem-sfb-condensed-support-derived-localization gives a^*j_!=0 on the item's module-object functors. One fault, C4 in step 3: it cited lem-sfb-dc-open-lower-shriek-preserves for bounded constructibility of j_!A. That node only gives the locally-finitely-presented notion of sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible. The item's Dctf and the Dctf/Dbc inputs of det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite (2) and -integral (3) need the finite-constant-local-model notion of sk-def-sfb-constructible. det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model says the converse implication fails, for example for Z_ell. I repaired step 3 in fixes/dag/nodes/sec-six-functors-basics/lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero.json. It now argues H^q(j_!A)=j_!H^q(A) by exactness, then cites the existing reviewed node lem-sf-open-extension-zero-constant-model-constructible for constant-model constructibility. The lfp inclusion needed by the rational node comes from det-def-sfb-constructible-local-model. The Tor-amplitude argument is kept. The lfp node is removed from uses, proof_deps and tool_uses, and the new tool_use is proposed. Steps 4-6 are correct after the repair. Clause (2) of the finite node and clause (3) of the integral and rational nodes cover exactly the admissible list (Z_ell = O_{Q_ell}, Q_ell = E). Only an object isomorphism is used, and R(r_Z)_* sends 0 to 0 by adjunction. Batch-5 flags on the three det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-* nodes are accepted. The path ends at def-trf-geometric-morphism, a general definition. The rest of the trf/pod closure is generic infrastructure (point systems, localization). Proper base change is a general six-functor theorem, not a step of the trace formula or Poincare duality, and the blueprint's own sk-prop-proper-base-change-unbounded route reduces to these same Dctf nodes. The declared tool uses are accepted. Full checks are in review.md.; 1 file(s) fixed by the reviewer
